summary: Iteration 10 — ffmpeg MOV->MP4 conversion successfully moved OUT of HTTP request into background task. 9/9 backend tests PASS in 7.4s. Legacy POST /api/analyses with .mov filename returned in 0.21s (status=processing); chunked POST /api/analyses/finalize with .mov filename returned in 0.15s (status=processing). Both are far under the ~10s SLO and ~100s Cloudflare origin-timeout. Background task settled the analyses to status=failed within ~0-2s of polling — expected because fake random bytes make ffmpeg/Gemini fail — proving the detached pipeline ran to completion and updated the doc without crashing the server. Regressions verified: finalize returns 400 for unknown upload_id, 400 for incomplete chunks; /api/plans returns 200; static site at / returns 200 HTML. All test-created analyses (5) and their disk files cleaned up in module teardown. NOTE: backend.err.log shows gemini-2.0-flash is now 404-deprecated at Google (see minor issues) — not a blocker for this iteration's fix, but WILL cause every real user analysis to end up 'failed' unless gemini-2.5-pro succeeds first.

minor.issue: Model fallback list includes 'gemini-2.0-flash', which now returns HTTP 404 from Google: 'This model models/gemini-2.0-flash is no longer available.' If gemini-2.5-pro also fails (e.g. schema/quota/rate-limit), the whole analysis goes to status=failed. Replace 2.0-flash with a supported fallback such as 'gemini-2.5-flash' or 'gemini-1.5-flash-latest'. Not blocking iter 10 (ffmpeg fix is verified), but blocking end-to-end user success on real clips.
Still no per-user cap on # of open upload_id dirs or cumulative chunk bytes on disk; no janitor task. Consider background purge of /app/backend/uploads/chunks/*/* older than ~2h.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py:_finalize_and_start_analysis (713-853) correctly inserts the doc synchronously (client can immediately GET /api/analyses/{id}) and schedules the heavy work via asyncio.create_task(_run_analysis_in_background(...)). HTTP response now returns in 0.15-0.25s regardless of video format — Cloudflare 520 cause is eliminated.

server.py:_convert_to_mp4_if_needed (856-914) uses subprocess_exec (non-blocking), -threads 1 (respects 0.05 vCPU pod), asyncio.wait_for(timeout=600) with kill+communicate() cleanup on timeout, and falls back to the original file on any failure. Good defensive coding.

server.py:_run_analysis_in_background (917-966) has separate try/except around conversion (falls through to AI even if conversion fails) and around AI (marks status=failed with user-friendly summary). No path leaves the doc stuck in 'processing' forever.

asyncio.create_task without holding a reference is generally frowned upon (garbage collector can drop the task); consider storing tasks in a module-level set OR migrate to FastAPI's BackgroundTasks. Low risk here because uvicorn keeps the loop alive.
server.py is now 1612 lines — still worth splitting into routers/analyses.py, routers/uploads.py, routers/payments.py etc. Carry-over from iter 9.

rca_of_issue: Cloudflare 520 root cause 2 (this iteration): ffmpeg MOV->MP4 conversion was running inline inside POST /api/analyses[/finalize] on a 0.05 vCPU / 128MB pod. On real .mov clips this exceeded Cloudflare's ~100s origin timeout, causing 520 even though the small chunked uploads themselves worked. Fix: moved _convert_to_mp4_if_needed into _run_analysis_in_background (scheduled via asyncio.create_task). Verified reproduction: with old code path, a .mov POST would block for ffmpeg's runtime; with the new code path, response returned in 0.21s (legacy) / 0.15s (finalize). Background task then updated video_path/mime_type on the doc and settled status to failed (fake bytes) or ready (real clips) without ever touching the HTTP response.
